observation.visible_scene: A close-up, vertically oriented sparkler held against a uniformly out-of-focus gray background. The lower section is a pink/magenta coated handle; the upper section is a dark gray/black pyrotechnic coating. The active burning front sits at the junction between the pink and black parts, showing a small orange-yellow flame that flickers and ejects bright sparks. The composition is stable throughout, with the stick roughly centered and tilted slightly.
visible_changes: A small orange flame persists at the pink/black junction in every frame, varying slightly in size and shape frame to frame.

Bright sparks are emitted intermittently: some frames (e.g. 1, 3, 13, 22, 26, 30, 33, 39) show multiple sparks arcing outward to the left and right, while other frames (e.g. 4, 6, 7, 8, 14, 18) show few or none, indicating a flickering, not continuous, spark shower.

The burning front and the stick drift only a few pixels vertically within the frame across the excerpt; the black coated length above the flame and the pink length below it remain broadly similar, with no dramatic shortening visible.
Faint wisps of smoke occasionally rise from the flame (e.g. frames 14, 20, 21).
The blurred gray background stays essentially static, with no scene change or new objects entering.
outside_clip_unknowns: Who is holding the sparkler and how it is gripped (the handle base is cut off at the bottom edge).
When the sparkler was lit and how much unburnt coating remains beyond this segment.
The full burn-out or final extinguishing of the sparkler.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight vertical shift of the flame/stick is real consumption of the coating or small hand/camera motion cannot be resolved from the blurred static background.
The exact rate at which the black coating is consumed is not clearly measurable over this short excerpt.
Spark trajectories are short streaks; their emission direction varies frame to frame and is not consistent.
